channel.description: Latest articles from Santa Monica Daily Press (smdp.com)

item.title: LA28 ticket registrations top 5 million with March deadline approaching
item.description: Over 5 million people from 194 countries registered for 2028 Los Angeles Olympics tickets. Registration closes March 18 for first ticket draw.

item.title: Ex-Los Angeles fire chief sues the city over her firing after the Palisades Fire
item.description: Former Los Angeles fire chief sues city, claiming her firing after the deadly Palisades Fire was politically motivated and unfair.

item.title: March at the Market
item.description: Santa Monica's Main Street and Pico farmers markets host spring events in March 2026, featuring live music, kids activities, and fresh greens.

item.title: Justice Department suit accuses UCLA of failing to protect Jewish employees from campus hostility
item.description: Justice Department sues UCLA, alleging it failed to protect Jewish employees from campus hostility and antisemitic harassment.

item.title: Live to Serve: A Visionary Series on Transformation, Service, and Returning to One’s Calling at The Crow
item.description: Michelle Edgar's three-part spoken word series 'Live to Serve' begins March 1 at The Crow Santa Monica, preparing for TEDx UCLA July 26.

item.title: Malibu Council Directs Staff to Pursue Two-Step Voting Process for $125 Million Sewer Project
item.description: Malibu City Council unanimously approved a two-step voting process for a $125 million sewer project to help 461 fire-damaged beachfront properties rebuild after the Palisades Fire.

item.title: Around Town: Frieze Art, Padel Courts, & Greens Fest
item.description: Santa Monica weekend events include Frieze LA art fair at Santa Monica Airport, Black History Greens Festival, new padel courts opening, and more.

item.title: City Acquires Emerging Artist's Work Through Frieze Partnership, Debuts Temporary Public Art
item.description: Santa Monica adds Erica Mahinay's 'Unfetter (Blue Gaze)' to municipal Art Bank through Frieze LA partnership. Temporary public art on display through March 1.
